Subject-Level Event Status for Start/Stop Data

Source: R/subject_folds.R
add_subject_status.Rd

Adds one event indicator per subject to long (start/stop, counting-process) data: `1` when any of the subject's rows has an event, `0` otherwise. Every row of a subject carries the same value, so it can stratify grouped folds, e.g. `rsample::group_vfold_cv(group = subject_id, strata = subject_status)`, which keeps the share of subjects with an event close to equal across folds.

Usage

add_subject_status(
  data,
  subject_id,
  status,
  event = 1,
  name = "subject_status"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per interval.

subject_id

The subject identifier column, as a string.

status

The event column, as a string.

event

The value of `status` that marks an event (default `1`). A factor or character `status` is matched on its labels, so a factor with levels `"0"`/`"1"` works as is, and one with levels `c("censored", "event")` needs `event = "event"` (an `event` that is not a label is an error). A logical `status` counts `TRUE` as the event (`event` must be logical, or a value that coerces to logical without producing `NA`, e.g. `1`/`0`). A numeric `status` needs a numeric or logical `event`.

name

The name of the new column (default `"subject_status"`). It must not already exist in `data`.

Value

`data` with an integer column `name` added.

See also

[subject_vfold_cv()], [subject_nested_cv()]

Examples

long <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3), status = c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0))
add_subject_status(long, "id", "status")
#>   id status subject_status
#> 1  1      0              1
#> 2  1      1              1
#> 3  2      0              0
#> 4  2      0              0
#> 5  3      0              0
